chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abd al-Rahman, who said:

I asked Aba Abd Allah عليه السلام about a group of people who drown in a ship, or a house falls upon them and they die, and it is not known which of them died before the other. He said: “Some of them inherit from others.”

key_terms.لَا يُعْلَمُ أَيُّهُمْ مَاتَ قَبْلَ صَاح: The order of death is unknown, which is the central legal issue in the report.
key_terms.يَغْرَقُونَ فِي السَّفِينَةِ: They drown in a ship; a case of collective accidental death.
key_terms.يَقَعُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْبَيْتُ: A house collapses upon them; another example of sudden shared death.
key_terms.يُوَرَّثُ بَعْضُهُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ: They inherit from one another; the legal ruling given in the hadith.

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance ruling when people die together and it is unclear who died first?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning people who die together in a shared disaster when the order of death is unknown. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that they inherit from one another, making it a foundational text in the law of inheritance for simultaneous or uncertain deaths.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5656 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdur Rahman who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a group of people who drown in a ship or a house collapses on them, causing their death, and it is not known who among them died first.
Imam (as) said: "They inherit from one another."
